record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: Let k be a field, let X be an affine scheme over k with coordinate algebra A, and let a be a finite-dimensional k-algebra. Suppose an algebraic group Γ, rather than only a finite group, acts completely reducibly on both A and a by automorphisms. For the equivariant map algebra M(X,a)^Γ, defined as the fixed-point algebra (a ⊗ A)^Γ for the diagonal Γ-action, classify its irreducible finite-dimensional representations.

evidence.quote: The action of Γ on X induces an action on the coordinate ring A of X. Then M = (a ⊗ A)Γ , the fixed points of the diagonal action of Γ on a ⊗ A.

(a) More general groups Γ. Instead of a finite group Γ, one can consider, for instance, an algebraic group acting completely reducibly on A and a. The first step in the study of the resulting EMAs would be to classify their irreducible finite- dimensional representations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be an affine scheme over $k$ with coordinate algebra $A = \mathcal{O}(X)$. Let $\mathfrak{a}$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra (for instance, a Lie algebra). Let $\Gamma$ be an algebraic group over $k$ acting on $X$ (hence on $A$) and on $\mathfrak{a}$ by $k$-algebra automorphisms, and assume that the induced $\Gamma$-actions on $A$ and on $\mathfrak{a}$ are completely reducible (i.e., each is a direct sum of finite-dimensional irreducible rational $\Gamma$-submodules). Form the diagonal action of $\Gamma$ on the tensor product $\mathfrak{a} \otimes_k A$, and define the equivariant map algebra
$$M(X,\mathfrak{a})^{\Gamma} := (\mathfrak{a} \otimes_k A)^{\Gamma},$$
the fixed-point subalgebra. Classify, up to isomorphism, all irreducible finite-dimensional representations of $M(X,\mathfrak{a})^{\Gamma}$; in particular, determine to what extent every such irreducible representation arises as a tensor product of evaluation representations (at $\Gamma$-orbits in the rational points of $X$) with one-dimensional representations, as in the case where $\Gamma$ is finite.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of irreducible finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map algebras is known when Γ is a finite group acting on X and on the target algebra (Neher–Savage–Senesi, 2009, and follow-ups on extensions, block decompositions, and the superalgebra case). The generalization to arbitrary algebraic groups Γ acting completely reducibly does not appear to have been carried out in the literature; available sources continue to treat the finite-group setting, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Irreducible finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map algebras
status_evidence.snippet: All irreducible finite-dimensional representations are tensor products of evaluation representations and one-dimensional representations (for finite Γ).
status_evidence.claim: The finite-group case is solved, supporting that the algebraic-group generalization is a distinct open problem.

status_evidence.title: Extensions and block decompositions for finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map algebras
status_evidence.snippet: The irreducible finite-dimensional representations were classified in [NSS12] for X affine of finite type and Γ finite.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work still assumes Γ finite, indicating the algebraic-group case is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Irreducible modules for equivariant map superalgebras and their extensions
status_evidence.snippet: Γ is a finite abelian group acting freely on the rational points of X.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations published since the survey continue to take Γ finite.
